method: One minimal live chat call (model openai/gpt-oss-120b, 75 prompt tokens, 8 completion tokens) through the Groq connector's own call path; the applied rate-limit headers returned by api.groq.com for Ben's authenticated organisation are recorded verbatim. No key material is recorded or was exposed.
reading: CORRECTED at Vane's release examination (INDEX 259): x-ratelimit-limit-requests: 1000 is the DAILY request limit (RPD), not per-minute — Groq documents that header as the daily limit; the published Free-plan baseline is 30 RPM, 1,000 RPD and 8,000 TPM. The applied token limit is 8,000 tokens per minute — the published Free-plan TPM figure for this model. The binding constraint for attempt 7 is the per-minute token budget: a package must fit, with its completion, inside the tokens available in its minute, or the provider answers 429 (a provider failure, recorded as such — never as successful retrieval or completion). Attempt 6's calls were small and fast; the passed design's captured packages (10,831-20,087 bytes) sit in the few-thousand-token range; a maximum-configuration package (~36,000 retrieved bytes) would exceed the minute budget on its own and is a bound for the design, not a shape the real run should approach.
